title: Helix · [O III] 5007 Å · core E–W slit

figure.extraction: Extract the unresampled JPEG ASCII85 stream from source archive fig9.eps using source-figure.ts. This is the original published raster, not a screenshot or fitted model.
figure.pixelConvention: Origin at top left, x right, y down; values are manually read centroid locations in the original 512 by 775 raster.
figure.readoutNote: Sparse manual digitization of visible centroid markers, not complete raw spectra. Readout precision is about ±0.8 arcsec and ±0.6 km/s, not a statistical measurement uncertainty. Published error bars vary and have not been transcribed; no chi-square or confidence interval is justified. Retain the whole published figure for visual checking.

slit.direction: E–W through the central star; negative offsets east, positive west as mapped by Fig. 9
slit.instrumentNote: MES/AAT; 70 micrometre slit, equivalent spectral width 6 km/s; profiles co-added in blocks of 5 of 512 increments over 163 arcsec (§2.2.2). Compare fitted centroids only. Do not use 6 km/s as centroid error, or synthesize a line profile without instrumental and thermal broadening.

systemic.source: Meaburn2005 §3.1, published systemic heliocentric velocity including systematic calibration uncertainty; subtracted once from every observed velocity. We do not rederive it from Table 1's internally inconsistent wavelength text.

defaultEvidence: 120 arcsec is half the approximate 240 arcsec separation of the inner [O III] brightness peaks (§2.2.2); it is a projected scale, not a measured 3D radius.
12.5 ±1.0 km/s is the paper's inferred inner-shell radial expansion from the central 25 km/s splitting (§3.1); here it initializes the equatorial speed of an explicit homologous expansion hypothesis.

Depth ratio 1 and inclination 0 degrees define an authored spherical baseline. Neither is a measured inner-shell depth or inclination. The 37 degree bipolar-axis tilt elsewhere in the paper is not assigned to this shell.
limitations: Only the inner-shell hypothesis is predicted. All sampled centroid branches remain visible, including faster components it cannot explain; no point is rejected to improve agreement.

The shell is optically thin, infinitesimally thin and centered on the slit origin. Velocity is radially outward and proportional to distance from its center. Neither homology nor front/back membership is determined by photographs.

This is an independent literature-scale hypothesis, not the joint image-derived shape cloud. The ESO images provide morphology and emissivity clues, not measured gas velocities; line-specific emissivity is not recovered from RGB colors.

Inclination is the shell polar-axis angle from the line of sight, tilted toward west within the slit plane. Equatorial radius is adjusted to retain the 120 arcsec projected extent along this slit; north–south extent is not constrained by this experiment.
2008 §2 corrects 2005 halo Figs. 3–5 slit zero points, not Fig. 9. Reference: https://academic.oup.com/mnras/article/384/2/497/1024027 . Do not apply that -26.1 km/s correction to this core slit.
Inclination cannot affect a sphere; depth and speed remain degenerate with one slit. RMS is a descriptive nearest-surface discrepancy, not a fitted likelihood or unique reconstruction.

textCrossCheck.source: §2.2.2 lists these approximate central components in prose; retained separately as a cross-check, not added as duplicate measurements.
